problem: The consumer MLINESTYLE metadata stored only fill ACI and partial element color. A from-scratch probe with nondefault extended fill/element CMC state exported an MLINESTYLE successfully because the bridge discarded those fields before the current codec could reject their loss.
implementation: Capture and restore fill truecolor, method, flags, raw index and color/book names, plus element method, flags, raw index and color/book names. Compile-time overload detection keeps the bundled codec, which does not expose those fields, source-compatible. The previously preserved element truecolor continues to be copied. The generated binary-input test closes its input stream before removing its scratch file for platform portability.
validation: On the current installed codec, the focused test passes 67 assertions: ordinary and explicit representable ByLayer styles export; extended fill and element state are stored exactly; each of the six extended fields on each side independently causes a refusal with the existing destination retained; combined-state controls retry successfully with the same filter.
The bundled-codec build compiles and its ordinary-style control passes two assertions; it does not expose the newer fields and does not claim to test them.
The installed-codec LTYPE, PR #3269 and MLEADERSTYLE CTests pass. The bundled fast LTYPE selection passes 29 cases and 4321 assertions with both generated ODA R13 inputs.
The standalone libdxfrw MLINESTYLE validation, CMC retention and body-transaction tests pass.

The consumer patch applies after the preceding 41 patches and all three changed files match the committed local candidate. Source-release inventory and its 18-control self-test pass for 1248 files. No drawing fixture was added.
limits: This is in-memory generated metadata and focused macOS consumer testing, not producer-authored DWG/CMC evidence, complete MLINESTYLE graph closure, DWG output qualification, GUI, non-macOS platforms, plugin ABI, or upstream integration. Partial intermediate codec APIs are not separately qualified. The R13 cross-version object-graph refusal remains open. No phase gate or support claim is promoted.
